result.title: Towards Reconstructing and Recognizing Objects behind Fragmented Occlusion using Video
result.summary: Perceiving objects through fragmented occlusions, such as foliage, is a natural capability of the human visual system but remains a fundamental challenge for computer vision. This work addresses the problem of object reconstruction, or de-occlusion, in the presence of high-density, fragmented occlusions. We propose a reconstruction framework that operates on a sequence of grayscale images of a moving object, acquired by a single camera, either stationary or in motion. The algorithm estimates the object's relative positions across frames by jointly registering the images and optimizing the alignment parameters to maximize the contrast of their average, referred to as the integrated image. This integrated image serves as the reconstructed representation of the object. Experimental evaluations on both synthetic and real video sequences demonstrate the feasibility of accurate reconstruction under occlusion densities exceeding 90%. The proposed approach is competitive with synthetic aperture techniques, which are limited to static objects and require complex camera setup with careful calibration. Furthermore, we show that the integrated image enables reliable object classification under severe occlusion when used as input to standard, off-the-shelf classifiers.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究高密度碎片化遮挡（如树叶）下的物体重建与识别：对单相机拍摄的运动物体灰度视频序列做联合配准，通过最大化平均图对比度估计帧间相对位移，得到去遮挡的「integrated image」作为重建表示，并输入现成分类器验证可识别性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其跨帧累积视觉证据以恢复被遮挡细节的思路，可能与 LVR 关注的视觉细节保留与证据筛选问题相关；但方法属传统配准优化，不涉及模型内部状态或 latent 推理生成，仅可供核查是否可作为视觉证据聚合的预处理或评价参照。
